text:
The Devils made the season's biggest swing on Oct. 23, trading for Connor Hellebuyck after his standoff in Winnipeg, and the team has looked like it believed the message. New Jersey is 4-1-0 in its last five, outscoring teams 23-14, and it earned it: 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) across those games and the better chances in four of them. Over the whole season the Devils have taken 57% of the five-on-five chances, which is the kind of number contenders post. Hellebuyck has been good rather than spectacular in his seven games (.916, +2.4 goals saved above expected), and last time out he needed 43 saves in a 7-4 win in Washington.

Montreal is the opposite case. The Canadiens sit at 28 points while our expected-points measure has them closer to 22, and the gap has a name: Jacob Fowler. The rookie is at .923 and +12.4 goals saved above expected in 13 games, and he is a big reason the Canadiens' results are running ahead of chances that have them at 48% of the expected goals. Fowler has needed to be that good. The injury list now holds Ivan Demidov (ankle), Chris Kreider, Josh Anderson and Mike Matheson, and the Canadiens have scored one goal in each of their last three losses. Zachary Bolduc has moved onto the first power-play unit and Cole Caufield is up to almost 21 minutes a night.

The matchup to watch is special teams. New Jersey's power play ranks sixth in the chances it creates, Montreal's penalty kill ranks 28th in chances allowed, and the Canadiens take 4.9 penalties a game. Eric Engels of Sportsnet wrote after Monday's loss that the power play Nick Suzuki called "definitely not broken" that morning was shattered by night's end.

Our numbers lean New Jersey, 3.49 expected goals to 2.77. Jesper Bratt brings an eight-game point streak, Luke Evangelista is one goal from 50 in his career (and is our Sleeper, 54% for a point), and Juraj Slafkovský is without a goal in twelve games on 4.4 expected goals.
headline: Fowler keeps the Habs afloat, and the Devils come calling
